Consider the system of linear differential equations given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118512/assets/d66051007ab78d2727f3b501156878a369a04b24bca337ed587feb07935a1de7.svg)

Given that the solution to the system can be written as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118512/assets/bfd809b436c24efcb2e9934b1c36293dfecb4bf87ab41c05f8cbbb9d506ea34d.svg)

what is the value of $a+b?$
question.worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118512/assets/7e191da3b082da420622418962e7491a6e78b6ed8192259b9b50ec8040bbc525.svg)

Since $A$ is upper-triangular, the repeated eigenvalue is $\lambda=-4$ (of multiplicity two).
For this eigenvalue, we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118512/assets/fb833263882adc2422083c111e96b0e030263f93e4c0174082f0f57667b46e8e.svg)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118512/assets/fe33e849a0e3baa7e8547c9559f9c36e980b8e715cba6e26900eea5d815e9b30.svg)

Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda$ and only one linearly independent eigenvector $\mathbf v,$ the solution of the system of differential equations is given by

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = c_1\mathbf{v} e^{\lambda t}  + c_2 (\mathbf{v}  te^{\lambda t}  +  \mathbf{w}e^{\lambda t} \, ),
$$

where $\mathbf{w}$ is a solution to the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$

To find $\mathbf{w},$ we solve the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{v}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(A-\lambda I)w & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}-4+4 & 1 \\ 0 & -4+4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{w}_{1} \\ {w}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The last equality allows us to form the following system of equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118512/assets/2c443847a5559737066873593b399117c03e9c8141b403bc7f820c9ad493e2a9.svg)

So, we obtain

$$
w_2 = 1.
$$

The variable $w_1$ is a free variable. Setting $w_1 = 0,$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118512/assets/00b635d3858d38c41ad9e1bacb00ed4c6370b5e2112aa82faa6ef37a83209a6c.svg)

Therefore, the general solution is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118512/assets/d1911a797bfa5915fb1478c91dc007ca3f1419b1093180dfb08932a008337b6e.svg)

Finally, we see that $a=0, b=1,$ and $a+b=1.$
